knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 120)

## What this notebook does

We ask whether **armed conflict raises child wasting** (the prevalence of low
weight-for-height among under-fives). Wasting is the mirror image of stunting: it is
**acute** malnutrition — a *flow*, not a stock. Weight-for-height drops within weeks of
a shock and recovers within months. So, unlike stunting (see `4_analyze_stunting.Rmd`,
which uses a long cumulative-exposure window), wasting calls for a **short lag**, close
to the original design of
[Jawad et al. (2021, *PLOS Medicine*)](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371/journal.pmed.1003810).

The rest of the design matches our other Pillar 4 panels: country-year two-way fixed
effects, country-clustered standard errors, and — because conflict variation is
concentrated in few countries and the survey-only outcome is sparse — a **wild cluster
bootstrap** reported alongside the analytic standard errors. Exposure is **battle
deaths per 100,000 population** from UCDP GED, taken from the master panel built in
`1_build_master.R`. Lags are built on the full annual conflict grid, then
subset to survey-year rows, so the sparsity of the outcome never corrupts the lag.

```{r libraries}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)
library(broom)
library(fwildclusterboot)
```

## The data

```{r load}
master <- readRDS(here("data_derived", "pillar4_master.rds"))

setFixest_fml(..ctrls = ~ log_gdp_pc + age_dep_ratio + pct_urban + pop_density +
                male_schooling + temperature + rainfall + earthquake + drought)
ctrls <- c("log_gdp_pc", "age_dep_ratio", "pct_urban", "pop_density",
           "male_schooling", "temperature", "rainfall", "earthquake", "drought")

# One-year-lagged exposure, built on the full annual grid then carried to survey rows.
panel <- master |>
  arrange(iso3, year) |>
  mutate(lag1_bd_p100k = dplyr::lag(battle_deaths_p100k),
         log_gdp_pc    = log(gdp_pc),
         .by = iso3)
```

### The estimation sample

Survey-year rows with a defined one-year lag and complete covariates, dropping
singleton fixed-effect groups (a lone observation is perfectly absorbed by its own
fixed effect, contributes nothing to the within estimator, and breaks the bootstrap's
pre-processing).

```{r sample}
MakeSample <- function(data, yvar, xvars) {
  s <- data |>
    filter(year >= 1996,   # outcomes are analysed from 1996 on
           !is.na(.data[[yvar]]),
           if_all(all_of(c(xvars, ctrls)), \(x) !is.na(x)))
  repeat {
    n0 <- nrow(s)
    s <- s |>
      add_count(iso3, name = "n_iso") |> filter(n_iso >= 2) |>
      add_count(year, name = "n_yr")  |> filter(n_yr  >= 2) |>
      select(-n_iso, -n_yr)
    if (nrow(s) == n0) break
  }
  s |> mutate(iso3 = factor(iso3), year = factor(year))
}

df <- MakeSample(panel, "wast", "lag1_bd_p100k")
```

The estimation sample is **`r nrow(df)` survey-country-years** across
**`r n_distinct(df$iso3)` countries** and
**`r min(as.integer(as.character(df$year)))`–`r max(as.integer(as.character(df$year)))`**.
Wasting prevalence is in percentage points; `lag1_bd_p100k` is battle deaths per
100,000 in the year before the survey.

```{r summary-table}
df |>
  mutate(wast, lag1_bd_p100k, log_gdp_pc, pct_urban, male_schooling,
         .keep = "none") |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable") |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)), mean = mean(value), sd = sd(value),
            min = min(value), median = median(value), max = max(value)) |>
  mutate(across(mean:max, \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Primary model

Wasting on one-year-lagged conflict intensity plus covariates, with country and year
fixed effects and country-clustered standard errors.

```{r primary}
m_wast <- feols(wast ~ lag1_bd_p100k + ..ctrls | iso3 + year,
                data = df, cluster = ~iso3)
etable(m_wast, keep = "lag1_bd_p100k", headers = "Wasting (pp)")
```

## Inference: how many real clusters, and a wild cluster bootstrap

```{r cluster-diagnostic}
cl <- df |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  summarise(within_ss = sum((lag1_bd_p100k - mean(lag1_bd_p100k))^2),
            ever_exposed = any(lag1_bd_p100k > 0), .groups = "drop")

tibble(
  quantity = c("Countries (nominal clusters)",
               "Ever conflict-exposed in sample",
               "With within-country exposure variation (identifying)",
               "Effective number of clusters (Herfindahl)"),
  value = c(nrow(cl),
            sum(cl$ever_exposed),
            sum(cl$within_ss > 1e-12),
            round(sum(cl$within_ss)^2 / sum(cl$within_ss^2), 1))
)
```

```{r boottest}
set.seed(1); dqrng::dqset.seed(1)
bt_wast <- boottest(m_wast, param = "lag1_bd_p100k", clustid = ~iso3,
                    fe = "year", B = 9999, type = "webb")

analytic <- coeftable(m_wast)["lag1_bd_p100k", ]
tibble(
  method   = c("Analytic (country-clustered)", "Wild cluster bootstrap (Webb)"),
  estimate = round(c(analytic["Estimate"], bt_wast$point_estimate), 4),
  p_value  = round(c(analytic["Pr(>|t|)"], bt_wast$p_val), 4),
  ci_low   = round(c(confint(m_wast)["lag1_bd_p100k", 1], bt_wast$conf_int[1]), 4),
  ci_high  = round(c(confint(m_wast)["lag1_bd_p100k", 2], bt_wast$conf_int[2]), 4)
)
```

## How long does the effect last? Lag profile (0–8 years)

To confirm wasting behaves as an *acute* outcome, we trace the coefficient on conflict
entered at each lag $k = 0…8$ in its own model (the `sw()` stepwise operator, as in the
mortality analysis). For a flow outcome we expect an effect concentrated at the short
lags that fades quickly — the opposite of stunting's slow, persistent stock response.
Lags are computed on the full annual panel via `fixest::l()`; each model uses its own
available survey sample.

```{r lag-profile, fig.height=4.5}
lagpanel <- master |>
  arrange(iso3, year) |>
  mutate(log_gdp_pc = log(gdp_pc),
         # analyse surveys from 1996 on; earlier rows only supply lagged exposure
         wast = if_else(year >= 1996, wast, NA))

lags_str <- paste0("l(battle_deaths_p100k, ", 0:8, ")", collapse = ", ")
fml <- as.formula(sprintf("wast ~ sw(%s) + %s | iso3 + year",
                          lags_str, paste(ctrls, collapse = " + ")))

fit <- feols(fml, data = lagpanel, panel.id = ~iso3 + year, cluster = ~iso3)

lag_profile <- imap(fit, \(mod, i) {
  tidy(mod, conf.int = TRUE) |>
    filter(str_detect(term, "battle_deaths_p100k")) |>
    mutate(lag = as.integer(str_extract(term, "(?<=, )[0-9]+")))
}) |> list_rbind()

ggplot(lag_profile, aes(lag, estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.15, fill = "#c1121f") +
  geom_line(colour = "#c1121f", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#c1121f") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:8) +
  labs(title = "Effect of conflict on wasting by years since exposure",
       subtitle = "Coefficient on battle deaths per 100k lagged k years, 95% CI (analytic)",
       x = "Years since conflict (lag)", y = "Effect on wasting (pp)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

## Robustness: logit-transformed prevalence

```{r robust-logit}
df_logit <- df |> mutate(wast_logit = qlogis(wast / 100))
m_logit  <- feols(wast_logit ~ lag1_bd_p100k + ..ctrls | iso3 + year,
                  data = df_logit, cluster = ~iso3)
set.seed(1); dqrng::dqset.seed(1)
bt_logit <- boottest(m_logit, param = "lag1_bd_p100k", clustid = ~iso3,
                     fe = "year", B = 9999, type = "webb")
etable(m_logit, keep = "lag1_bd_p100k", headers = "Wasting (logit)")
cat(sprintf("Wild cluster bootstrap: p = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            bt_logit$p_val, bt_logit$conf_int[1], bt_logit$conf_int[2]))
```

## Interpretation and caveats

- **What we find.** Net of fixed country and year differences, the one-year-lagged
  conflict coefficient on wasting is small and **not statistically distinguishable from
  zero**, and the wild cluster bootstrap widens the interval further. The logit check
  agrees. At the country-average, survey-only level we do not find robust evidence that
  conflict raises wasting.
- **The lag profile behaves as expected for a flow.** Whatever short-lag signal exists
  does not build or persist across years — consistent with wasting being acute and
  recoverable, and in deliberate contrast to the slow, persistent shape one would look
  for in a stunting (stock) response.
- **Ecological design.** This identifies national associations, not individual causal
  effects; micro-level studies routinely find sharp wasting spikes in acute crises that
  a country-average annual panel can miss.
- **Few clusters.** The effective number of identifying clusters is well below the
  nominal country count, so power is limited; the bootstrap makes that explicit.
- **Data caveats carried from the master build:** exposure begins in 1989 (the first
  year of UCDP GED coverage); competing survey values per country-year were resolved
  on methodology upstream in `1_build_master.R`.
```
